name: Wanderlog Pro
subcategory: trip planning, navigation and travel intelligence
tagline: Build a collaborative itinerary from user-entered places, notes, and reservations

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited-looking trips, road-trip stops, collaborators, itinerary/map, notes, and budget entries; 0 offline access and 0 automatic Gmail scanning
tiers.notes: The official pages do not publish a numeric cap for attachments or trips.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited attachments, offline access, route optimization, live flight updates, automatic email scanning, and export
tiers.notes: Direct web pricing starts at $39.99/year; US App Store listings also show $49.99/$59.99 annual and $5.99/$16.99 monthly offers, so checkout/platform can change the price.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free plan: no published numeric cap on trips, stops, collaborators, or budget entries; 0 offline access and 0 automatic Gmail scanning.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; direct web annual price starts at $39.99, while app-store offers vary
pricing.hiddenCosts: Different storefronts expose materially different subscription offers. Hotel/activity booking links can earn Wanderlog commissions even on the free planner.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Wanderlog Pro, build a collaborative itinerary from user-entered places, notes, and reservations. The hard boundary is maps, travel data, collaboration, offline access, route optimization, and mobile apps, plus proprietary live data and network coverage.
coreLoopDIY: Build a collaborative trip itinerary from user-entered places, notes, and reservations, map them, and keep an offline copy without claiming live proprietary availability.
requirements: optional public transit or weather API
whatYouLose: maps, travel data, collaboration, offline access, route optimization, and mobile apps
booking, disruption support, and offline map fleet
moatNotes: proprietary live data and network coverage
ongoingBurden: map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Wanderlog Pro because travel subscriptions sell current data and confidence during disruption, not just an itinerary list. The recurring cost buys map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Wanderer
priorArt.desc: Open-source self-hosted trail database and route explorer using open map data.

alternatives.name: TREK
alternatives.desc: A collaborative itinerary with maps, reservations and offline PWA support; Docker is the boarding pass.

alternatives.name: AdventureLog
alternatives.desc: A collaborative itinerary with maps, reservations and checklists; the server is now part of the trip.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Furkot
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It looks free until enough map use; then editing locks until a $14-a-year Pass.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal itinerary organizer DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Wanderlog Pro in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, MapLibre GL, and user-supplied map and travel APIs; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build a collaborative trip itinerary from user-entered places, notes, and reservations, map them, and keep an offline copy without claiming live proprietary availability.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create trips, days, places, reservations, notes, documents, packing items, and emergency contacts.
Geocode only user-entered places and display them through MapLibre with cached trip-area tiles where allowed.
Parse forwarded reservation text locally into editable fields without logging message content.
Build a day timeline, route overview, conflict warnings, timezone display, and offline printable itinerary.
Allow manual updates for delays and reservations and label all external data with source and timestamp.
Export a complete trip bundle as JSON, calendar file, Markdown, and PDF.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out live flight, hotel, award, or ticket inventory.
Deliberately leave out commercial turn-by-turn navigation and global offline maps.
Deliberately leave out booking guarantees, disruption rebooking, and traveler support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
